title: Fermion bag study of the two-dimensional Majorana-Hubbard model at finite hopping
abstract: The two-dimensional Majorana-Hubbard model on the $π$-flux lattice involves the most local interaction possible for a lattice with one relativistic Majorana fermion per site. It is predicted to host a Majorana semimetal, dimerized phases, and quantum-critical points with an emergent $U(1)$ symmetry. Nonperturbative lattice calculations for this model remain a major open challenge, thus far limited to zero hopping. We present quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the model at finite hopping using Hamiltonian fermion bags, which are based on a continuous-time expansion with Boltzmann weights that are Pfaffians of a matrix with dimension set by the expansion order, and which give the sign of the weight. Sign problem severity is related to the location of zero modes in the free hopping matrix, and for couplings $g\lesssim 0.7$ and $β=L/4$ it is fully removed for lattices up to at least $256$ sites. The interaction strength $g>0$ enhances the $U(1)$-charged dimerization doublet and suppresses the neutral channel, as the renormalization group predicts. Increasing the interactions also restores $U(1)$ symmetry in the component of the dimerization correlator that is even under bond orientation exchange, but not its odd component. There is a persistent anisotropy in the odd component with the symmetry of a lattice nematic. The data is consistent with a gapless semimetal throughout the sign-problem-minimal window.
summary: This work tackles the computationally difficult problem of simulating the 2D Majorana-Hubbard model at finite hopping using advanced Quantum Monte Carlo methods based on Pfaffians. The authors successfully remove the sign problem for a significant parameter range and find that the system remains a gapless semimetal, confirming theoretical predictions about its electronic structure.
main_problem: The primary challenge is performing nonperturbative lattice calculations for the two-dimensional Majorana-Hubbard model at finite hopping, which was previously limited to zero hopping.
main_result: The simulations consistently show that the system remains in a gapless semimetal phase across the sign-problem-minimal parameter window, confirming the expected behavior.
method: Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations are employed using novel Hamiltonian fermion bags, which utilize Pfaffians derived from a continuous-time expansion to manage the sign problem.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional Majorana-Hubbard model defined on a $\pi$-flux lattice, involving one relativistic Majorana fermion per site. The Hamiltonian includes hopping terms ($t$) and interaction terms ($g$).
key_observables: Dimerization correlators (charged doublet vs. neutral singlet), the average sign, and the free-fermion spectrum $\epsilon(\mathbf{k})$ showing Dirac points.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($g/t$), hopping parameter ($t$), and lattice size/inverse temperature ($ eta=L/4$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the Pfaffian calculation being stable and successfully removing the sign problem for couplings $g \lesssim 0.7$ and specific $ eta$ values.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $\pi$-flux lattice structure, the free-fermion spectrum with Dirac points, and the evolution of the average sign and correlation functions as a function of interaction strength $g/t$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the model and the computational difficulty (sign problem), details the Hamiltonian fermion bag QMC method using Pfaffians, presents results showing sign-problem removal, and concludes by analyzing the symmetry and gapless nature of the resulting semimetal.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of advanced QMC techniques (Pfaffians) to a model featuring Majorana fermions and emergent symmetries provides deep insights into topological phases relevant to condensed matter physics.
